content.title: About
content.content: Cheese pizza is a popular fast‑food item consisting of a medium‑thick crust topped with tomato sauce and a generous layer of melted cheese. It is commonly served in quick‑service restaurants and pizzerias, baked until the cheese turns golden and bubbly.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese pizza is one of the best‑selling items in fast‑food chains worldwide.
Traditional cheese for pizza is mozzarella, but many places blend several cheeses for a richer flavor.
A medium crust (about 0.5–0.7 cm thick) provides a balance between a crisp edge and a soft interior.
In some countries the pizza is finished with extra herbs such as oregano or basil.
Cheese pizza often serves as a base for additional toppings like pepperoni, ham, or vegetables.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheese topping is rich in calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Protein rich
items.content: Both the cheese and the dough provide a good amount of animal and plant protein for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Certain cheeses contain vitamin D, which aids calcium absorption.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Cheese pizza quickly replenishes energy thanks to the combination of carbohydrates in the crust and fats in the cheese.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Some cheese varieties contain live cultures that support a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Cheese pizza is calorie‑dense, so it should be eaten in moderation, especially for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese contains saturated fats, which can raise cholesterol levels if consumed excessively.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after eating cheese pizza.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Both cheese and sauce often contain significant sodium, which can be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to casein, the main protein in cheese.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese pizza is typically enjoyed hot, sliced into wedges. You can add fresh herbs, a drizzle of olive oil, or a spicy sauce to taste. It is often served with a side salad of fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftover pizza in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore a crisp crust.
